source_name: UNDP Procurement Notices — UNDP-MKD country office
why_relevant: UNDP North Macedonia procures individual consultants and firms directly by named role — e.g. 'IC 868-2026 National Sustainable Finance & Institutional Specialist'. IC notices are literally job postings for finance/institutional specialists embedded in government counterparts, and firm RFPs name delivery teams. High-signal for the jobs/hiring topic on the donor route.

source_name: IOM North Macedonia — Procurement / consultancy services
why_relevant: Another IO contracting authority in-country publishing consultancy calls; occasionally covers digital payments/cash-transfer and financial-inclusion work. Adds to the donor-route supplier and expert population.

source_name: Центар за граѓански комуникации (Center for Civil Communications, CCC) — public procurement monitoring
why_relevant: The long-running independent monitor of MK public procurement. Its semi-annual monitoring reports, municipal procurement database and case studies identify concentrated suppliers, single-bidder procedures and confidential contracts — an analytical pointer that tells you which suppliers and which buying units to track in ESJN, and which contracts were deliberately hidden.

source_name: data.gov.mk / opendata.mk — open data catalogues incl. procurement datasets
why_relevant: National open-data portal (280+ datasets, 50+ institutions) plus the civil-society opendata.mk mirror; ESJN 'Open Data' visualisations and CSV exports are referenced here. Gives a bulk, machine-readable route into award data instead of scraping the ASP.NET grids.

source_name: Commercial tender aggregators covering North Macedonia (DevelopmentAid, Hook/SellToState, GTBC, TendersInfo-type services)
why_relevant: Third-party services that normalise, translate and alert on MK notices and on donor tenders naming MK. Useful as a cross-check that a notice existed (and for historic notices removed from the source portal), and their sector taxonomies surface banking/payments tenders that keyword search misses. Content is mostly paywalled.

source_name: Slobodenpristap.mk / АСПИ — FOI request platform and register of information holders
why_relevant: Fallback route when a contract, award file or the contracting authority's staffing is not published: FOI requests to the named holder (e.g. DKZJN, MoF) are filed and answered in public, and the ASPI register lists every institution's information officer — itself a named-contact dataset for buying units.

source_name: G+D Netcetera — Careers / job listings (North Macedonia, Skopje / Bitola / Ohrid)
source_subtype: vendor careers page / ATS job board
why_relevant: Netcetera's Skopje delivery centre is one of the largest payments-engineering employers in MK (3-D Secure / digital payment security, used by 2,000+ banks and issuers globally). Individual job pages are country-tagged in the URL slug ('...-North-Macedonia-Skopje-...'), so the open-role set is directly countable over time as a capacity/hiring signal for MK payments engineering.

source_name: MASIT — Chamber of Commerce for ICT, member directory (Стопанска комора за информатички и комуникациски технологии)
why_relevant: Single richest actor-map pointer for the MK IT supplier ecosystem: ~160+ member companies each with a profile page carrying self-description of sectors served, including banking/fintech. This is how you enumerate integrators you have not yet heard of, in both MK and EN mirrors of the same directory.

source_name: CaSys — Интернационален Картичен Систем АД Скопје (independent card processor) corporate site
why_relevant: The only MK-domiciled card processor certified by Mastercard/Visa/Diners and approved by UnionPay; serves commercial banks and financial institutions as an outsourced processing supplier. Its news/blog and about pages reveal which banks and schemes it works with, new product launches, and organisational moves — the single best indirect window onto private banks' card-processing arrangements.

source_name: CaSys LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: CaSys posts MK-language announcements (product launches, scheme memberships, hiring) on LinkedIn earlier and more often than on its website; also surfaces staff-count and role-mix changes.

source_name: KIBS AD Skopje — ICT services / open banking platform (Клириншки интербанкарски системи)
why_relevant: KIBS is the interbank clearing house AND a supplier of digital-trust and open-banking platform services sold to MK banks and fintechs; its ICT services page names the platform products banks consume. Bank-side adoption of KIBS services is a supplier-side trace of private banks' technology choices, and KIBS also issues digital certificates used by e-banking of banks such as Stopanska banka.

source_name: Asseco SEE (ASEE) — news & events, regional case studies incl. North Macedonia
why_relevant: ASEE publicly documented running the Sparkasse / Ohridska banka merger integration in Macedonia — exactly the kind of supplier-side disclosure that names a private MK bank as a customer. Its news stream is the closest thing to a public record of core-banking/payments implementations at MK banks, and it also announces country-manager and org changes.

source_name: Sorsix International — company site and MASIT profile
why_relevant: Skopje-headquartered product/engineering firm whose MASIT profile states it has deployed solutions for banking customers (UK, Hong Kong, Australia) alongside healthcare/transport/retail/government. Large Skopje engineering base; its careers page and client references are a capacity and domain-competence signal for MK-based banking delivery.

source_name: Nextsense — jobs page and company profile (Skopje)
why_relevant: Skopje ICT solutions house explicitly positioning in digital transformation for government, telecom and FINANCE across Europe; ~88 employees at the Skopje location per third-party company data. Its jobs page is a direct hiring signal, and its solutions/clients pages are candidate customer references for MK financial institutions.

source_name: zk.mk — business directory category 'Банкарски Системи' (banking systems suppliers)
why_relevant: MK-language commercial directory with a dedicated 'Банкарски Системи' and 'Електронско Банкарство' category — a ready-made, local-language enumeration of firms that sell banking/e-banking systems in MK, including small local players invisible to English search. Ideal seed list for snowballing to vendor sites.

source_name: Duna — софтвер / solutions and references (duna.mk)
why_relevant: Long-established MK systems integrator and hardware/software supplier; its MK-language software and project/reference pages publish named delivery projects (e.g. the Assembly voting system). Reference and news pages are the mechanism by which any bank engagement would become visible, and its job ads indicate delivery capacity.

source_name: InterWorks (Bitola/Skopje) — corporate site and careers
why_relevant: Bitola-based MK integrator delivering to international enterprise clients; ISO 27001 certified. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE-SIGNAL VALUE: InterWorks publicly states a policy of NOT disclosing client references (to reduce social-engineering exposure) — so for this actor, hiring ads and leadership announcements are the only usable trace, and absence of references must not be read as absence of bank work.

source_name: Interspace — Клиенти и препораки (clients & references)
why_relevant: A dedicated MK-language 'clients and references' page from a provider that explicitly markets connectivity, secure optical links, VPN and dedicated cloud to banks, insurers and financial institutions. This is the canonical shape of the supplier-side reference page this cell exists to harvest.

source_name: Login Systems — banking-integration reference posts (Business Central + MK banks)
why_relevant: A partner-published MK-language reference post describing bank-integration functionality delivered for MK customers. Small ERP/integration partners publish this kind of named-bank detail far more freely than tier-1 vendors, making them a high-yield, low-competition source for who connects to which MK bank's rails.

source_name: Joberty North Macedonia — IT employer profiles and IT job feed
source_subtype: IT job board + employer review aggregator
why_relevant: Joberty launched an MK operation with 500+ employer reviews of MK tech companies and maintains per-company profile pages (e.g. G+D Netcetera, Nextsense) plus a sortable, date-ordered IT job feed. Gives cross-vendor, normalised hiring volume for exactly the Skopje delivery centres this cell tracks — a capacity signal that does not depend on each vendor's own careers page.

source_name: Vrabotuvanje.com.mk — general MK job board, Skopje / IT filters
why_relevant: The largest general MK job board; carries vendor and bank IT ads (observed roles include full-stack developers requiring banking/financial-systems experience and payment-card processing support). URL takes a location query parameter, so a Skopje+IT filtered feed is straightforward to poll for supplier-side payments hiring in MK terms.

source_name: Kariera.mk — employer pages and IT job listings
why_relevant: Second MK job board with per-employer landing pages for the vendors in this cell (Nextsense observed). Useful redundancy: vendors often post to one board and not the other, so single-board monitoring undercounts hiring.

source_name: IT.mk — Кариера section and MK tech news
why_relevant: MK tech-media outlet with a dedicated careers section and editorial coverage of local IT firms; the natural venue where a Skopje delivery centre's expansion, new country manager, or big bank project would be reported in Macedonian before (or instead of) any English release.

source_name: Inovativnost.mk — profiles of MK IT companies
why_relevant: MK-language outlet publishing long-form profiles of local IT firms (observed: a full profile of InterWorks, the Bitola integrator). Because integrators like InterWorks refuse to publish client references, this kind of interview-based press is often the only place delivery scope and leadership names appear.

source_name: Bankarstvo.mk — MK banking-sector news incl. bank & vendor job ads
why_relevant: MK-language banking vertical that republishes bank recruitment ads (Komercijalna, NLB, TTK, Silk Road, CCB) and carries vendor-adjacent items (e.g. CaSys prevention advisories, Komercijalna banka entering SEPA — an event that implies supplier work). Bridges the bank side and supplier side of this cell.

source_name: Ecommerce.mk (Асоцијација за е-трговија на Македонија) — payment-product announcements
why_relevant: MK e-commerce association publishing vendor payment-product news (observed: CaSys new payment products). Association members are merchants and PSPs, so its feed reveals acquiring/gateway supplier moves that never appear on bank websites.
